items.text: The birthday ceremony of Ali Mohammad Kord Kazemi, a 22-year-old basketball player, was held on September 17 at Behesht Zahra. He was shot dead on the night of January 9, 2026, during protests in Tehran. One attendee at the ceremony called for revenge against those responsible.

The US State Department has agreed to sell 48 F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia. Previously, the New York Times reported that US intelligence officials expressed concerns about possible Chinese espionage. The contract value is estimated at around $24 billion.

Russia and China used their veto power to block the extension of the expert panel's mandate monitoring Iran's sanctions at the UN Security Council. The UK representative stated that this veto does not affect existing sanctions. Restrictions related to Iran's arms programs remain in effect for all UN members.

Omid Memarian, political analyst, said that a planned meeting between a member of the New York mayor's office and the Islamic Republic's ambassador did not take place. He added that recent tensions are more of a reflection of political differences between the New York mayor and the Israeli government.

Jürgen Klopp appeared at the German national team press conference wearing a hat with the slogan "One of 83 million" and the Adidas logo in the colors of the German flag. He stated he wants to reclaim the flag for the people and not let national pride be taken by the wrong people. This act followed the far-right party's victory in the Saxony-Anhalt state elections.

Families of Hamidreza Hemmati and Habib Khoubipour lit candles in their memory. Habib Khoubipour, a 47-year-old math talent, was shot by government forces in Isfahan on January 8, 2026, and died after several days in hospital. Hamidreza Hemmati, a 21-year-old student, was kidnapped the same day and his body was returned to his family after a few days.

The US State Department announced that the Islamic Republic delegation will travel to New York next week to attend the UN General Assembly. The delegation members will face travel restrictions and a ban on purchasing luxury goods. It was also reported that Benjamin Netanyahu will not meet with Donald Trump but will meet with Marco Rubio.

On Wednesday, 25 Shahrivar, the home of Rahmatollah and Parvaneh Sabet, a Bahá'í couple living in Shiraz, was searched by security forces. Several personal belongings of the elderly couple were confiscated during the search. The couple, both over 80 years old, were threatened with imprisonment.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center reported a security incident in the Strait of Hormuz, 16 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman. The crew is safe and no environmental impact has been confirmed so far. Authorities are investigating, and vessels are advised to navigate cautiously.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations Center reported an incident involving a ship in the Strait of Hormuz. The crew is safe and no environmental impact has been confirmed. Authorities are investigating the incident and have urged passing ships to proceed with caution.

David Beckham, co-owner of Inter Miami, supported Lionel Messi and said Messi should win the Ballon d'Or. Beckham praised Messi's performance in the 2026 World Cup and his recent championships. He called Messi the best player of the World Cup and deserving of the Ballon d'Or.
On Wednesday, September 16, parts of Valencia experienced flooding. Vehicles slowly passed through flooded streets and a store was submerged. Local authorities had issued a rain and storm warning.

Seyed Ali Kazemi, spokesperson for the judiciary, announced that indictments have been issued for 159 senior political and military officials from the US and Israel. Among them, 92 are American and 67 are Israeli. This news was announced on September 17.

The US State Department sanctioned two entities and three individuals involved in Iran's digital asset networks. The targeted network includes BitBank, linked to Babak Zanjani, which transfers funds to the IRGC. The US stated it will continue efforts to prevent Iran from accessing financial resources.

Juventus defeated NEC Nijmegen 5-0 in their first match of the new Europa League season. Goals were scored by Nico Gonzalez, Alabakovich, Woltmade, Celik, and Kolo Muani. This victory came after a loss to Sassuolo in Serie A.

The US State Department has launched the 'Reward for Justice' program offering up to $15 million for information disrupting the financial mechanisms of the IRGC. The program stated that the IRGC uses digital asset exchanges for money laundering and financing its activities abroad. People are asked to submit any relevant information.

Debbie Hewitt requested in a letter to Gianni Infantino the release of documents related to the halted plan to sell part of the World Cup commercial rights before the FIFA Council meeting on October 15. She also asked for a written explanation regarding the lifting of the suspension of the US national team striker. The letter was also sent to FIFA's Secretary General and included criticisms about FIFA's governance.

Donald Trump stated that the war with the Islamic Republic is approaching a critical stage. He must soon decide on resuming extensive attacks and efforts to destroy the regime. The Pentagon has been tasked with maintaining the current level of US forces in the Middle East until the end of the year.

Alireza Namvar Haghighi said that rebuilding the Talqan 2 nuclear center does not necessarily mean a definite move by the Islamic Republic towards nuclear weapons and could be a leverage in negotiations. He warned that if the US and its allies interpret this as a step towards nuclear weapons, the likelihood of military action will increase.

The US State Department spokesperson announced that Iranian officials are not allowed to purchase luxury goods in New York. These restrictions are due to Iran's economic problems and the government's use of wealth to support proxy forces. Sellers in the New York area have also been asked not to participate in violating these bans.
Donald Trump is planning to meet with Delcy Rodriguez, the interim president of Venezuela. This meeting may take place next week. The news was reported by Axios.

The Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) announced that China has equipped its military base in Djibouti with new communication equipment. This equipment could enhance China's ability to gather intelligence and monitor military activities across the Middle East. It could also help China monitor the military forces of nearby countries and maintain communication with Chinese ships and aircraft operating in the region.

The White House rejected the UN independent fact-finding mission's report on the likelihood of war crimes committed by the US in the February 28 attacks on Iran. The mission stated that at least 178 civilians were killed in these attacks. The White House spokesperson said the Islamic Republic is the only party that committed war crimes.

Donald Trump stated that the Islamic Republic is not yet ready to reach an agreement and the US will only accept a deal it considers good. He said Iran's economy is in its worst condition with inflation over 300 percent. Trump also mentioned US control over the Strait of Hormuz and the destruction of Iran's radars.

Prince Reza Pahlavi held a virtual meeting with Australian opposition leaders to discuss Iran's situation and support for Iranians. He called for dialogue with the Australian government and expressed willingness to visit the country. The discussions focused on human rights, protection of Iranians, and economic relations prospects.

At around 12:30 AM on Friday, a shooting occurred near Daneshgah Street and Daneshjoo Street in Zahedan. One armed individual, three military personnel, and two female bystanders were injured in the incident. Security forces have been deployed at the scene, and the entrances and exits of Zahedan have been blocked.

Reuters reported that the Iran war will be one of the topics in the September 24 meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Washington. Economic, trade, and security disputes between the two countries will also be discussed. The Trump administration has not sanctioned Chinese banks but has warned about continued trade with Tehran.

The President of South Korea stated that the country will not send any military forces or equipment to the Middle East. The South Korean government is considering increasing its role in protecting shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The Foreign Minister had previously said no decision has been made about deploying forces.

Rania Al-Mashat stated that the war between the US and the Islamic Republic caused about 150 billion dollars in economic damage to Arab countries in the first month. She warned that the war could delay investment and economic diversification efforts in Arab countries. Al-Mashat called for preventing the expansion of the war and maintaining freedom of navigation.

The US Attorney's Office has moved to seize about $61 million in cryptocurrency from the sale of sanctioned Iranian oil. Part of the funds was transferred to networks linked to the IRGC. Miad Maleki, former head of the US Treasury's sanctions targeting office, said the case shows cryptocurrency has become a key route for evading sanctions.

Reza Arab referred to the meeting of Prince Reza Pahlavi with opposition leaders and Australian representatives. Pahlavi emphasized the Iranian people's right to determine their own destiny. He defined his role as a bridge during the transition to a national and modern government.

Hossein Taeb, head of the Basij Organization, announced that American forces will soon be defeated and leave the region. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic firmly defends the Strait of Hormuz and other strategic defensive capacities. Training courses to increase citizens' readiness in land, air, and sea fields are also being pursued.

Amir Giti, a journalist for Iran International, in analyzing Trump's remarks, said the US President meant not that Tehran does not want to negotiate, but that the Islamic Republic is not yet ready to make concessions on its nuclear program, the Strait of Hormuz, and its missile program. He added that US economic pressures and the closure of sanctions evasion routes put the Islamic Republic in a choice between negotiating for 'breathing room' or continuing economic conditions until 'melting away bit by bit'.

Sadegh Beigdeli referred to Donald Trump's statements about the Islamic Republic nearing collapse and said the pro-negotiation faction in the Islamic Republic currently does not have the upper hand. He hopes that after the November elections, the possibility of moving towards an agreement will be provided.

At the Janfadaian Iran gathering in Tehran, coffins with images of Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu were displayed. Attendees emphasized pursuing revenge against them for killing Ali Khamenei. Similar symbolic executions of these figures have been held in recent events.

Changes in US immigration policies have made the asylum path more difficult for Iranians. The acceptance rate for Iranian asylum cases has fallen to 38 percent this year. In 2026, no cases of Iranian Christian converts have been accepted.

The International Federation of Fitness and Bodybuilding did not recognize the recent election results of the Iranian bodybuilding federation due to violations and suspended the federation. The suspension was due to significant irregularities in the election assembly and unequal opportunities for candidates. The suspension will continue until conditions are corrected, but Iranian athletes can still participate in events through the IFBB executive committee members.

Amir Reza Nasrazadani, a former football player, has been sentenced to 26 years in prison and remains without leave. He was arrested during the 'Women, Life, Freedom' protests and faced the risk of execution. Nasrazadani suffered a severe hand injury and underwent surgery.

The wife of Parsa Loinian, along with other families of the missing, lit a candle in his memory. Parsa Loinian was a 31-year-old mechanic from Isfahan. He was killed by officers' bullets during the national revolution in January.

Farzin Nadimi, senior defense and security researcher at the Washington Institute, said equipping China's military base in Djibouti with new communications equipment could enable China to locate ships and monitor maritime movements, especially American forces. He added that analyzing signals and changes in radio traffic could help China identify changes in force posture and understand how American carrier groups operate.

Sara Regensburger's new collection titled "Diaspora, the Art of Belonging" was showcased at London Fashion Week. The collection combines modern Western design with elements of Iranian culture. It explores the experience of living between two cultures and the search for a sense of belonging.

Saudi Arabia, through Oman, has offered a two-week ceasefire and direct talks with the Houthis. The Houthis demand an end to the siege of Yemen and Saudi withdrawal from the country. Riyadh officials have reported the Houthis' intention to attack Marib and control the provinces of Marib and Jawf.

The 10-kilometer running race in Tehran was held on the morning of Friday, 27 Shahrivar, with thousands of men and women participating. Notably, women participated without mandatory hijab. Previously, the Mahan-run half marathon in Kerman was canceled due to protests.

The number of detainees in Urmia has increased to five. The detainees include Majid Ebtehaj, Vahed Shabani, Behdar Asadi, Saleh Darbubehchichak, and Farhang Dehghan. These arrests occurred on Wednesday, September 15.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin from Iran International spoke about the display of coffins with images of Trump and Netanyahu by supporters of the Islamic Republic in the streets. He said these displays do not replace real victory and that the Islamic Republic aims to create an illusion of victory.

A video shows that a child scavenging in the garbage in Bagestan fell into a municipal trash bin due to a lid problem. The child was searching for recyclable materials. This incident has been reported in the media.
Mam Aziz Qaderi, a citizen from Pasveh, was summoned and interrogated by the IRGC intelligence and then released. His home was also searched by security forces. This event occurred yesterday.

Alireza Salimi stated that the successes of the resistance front in Yemen have surprised the US and its allies. He said countries following the US will pay a heavy price. He also mentioned that the US has made miscalculations regarding Iran, Yemen, and Hezbollah.

Alireza Beiranvand intends to play for Esteghlal after completing his military service. He is scheduled to go to Shiraz for military service in early Mehr or Aban and plans to terminate his contract with Tractor before joining Fajr Sepasi. His service duration is reduced due to being married and is expected to finish by the end of the current season.

In the 'Jan-Fadaian Exercise' rally held on Friday, September 27, symbolic coffins with pictures of Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu were displayed. This video was published in the media of the Islamic Republic.

The military prosecutor of East Azerbaijan province announced the formation of a judicial case against police officers involved in a violent encounter with a teenager in Tabriz. These officers are currently in custody and investigations are ongoing. A video of the incident has been widely circulated on social media.

Mehdi Chamran, head of Tehran City Council, said that people of all ages and tastes have come to show their support for the country and the leader. He added that the enemy is on a downward slope and will face harsher setbacks if it continues.

A citizen criticized the increase in the price of Asentra medicine in a video sent to Iran International. He said that under these conditions, he cannot afford the cost of his psychiatric medications. This issue has raised concerns about access to essential medicines.

In a school in Isfahan, a teacher wearing a Basij military uniform appeared in class and imposed the government's repressive discourse on students. In Bandar Abbas, school officials informed families that students must attend school wearing war identification tags. These actions were reported following the December protests.

Benjamin Netanyahu stated at the Likud party's election campaign launch that overthrowing the Islamic Republic and completely destroying Hezbollah and Hamas are Israel's goals. He referred to Israel's military actions in Iran, Lebanon, Syria, and the Gaza Strip. These remarks were made during the Likud party's election campaign.

The IRGC and Basij are holding the military and security exercise "Sacrifices for Iran" in Tehran starting Friday morning. Paramilitary forces, regime supporters, and organized children and teenagers are participating in this exercise. This event coincides with the worsening economic crisis and growing public dissatisfaction.

The IRGC and Basij held a military and security exercise called "Sacrificers of Iran" in Tehran on Friday, September 27. The commander of Tehran's IRGC stated the exercise aims to counter enemy propaganda against the Islamic Republic. Paramilitary forces, Houthis, and Basij children also participated in the exercise.

Faezeh Dibaei, a discus throw athlete and member of the national para-athletics team, is facing equipment shortages. She has requested an electric wheelchair suitable for her physical condition. This need was raised ahead of the 2026 Para Asian Games in Nagoya.

Viewers have reported inefficiencies in insurance, unpaid premiums, and the termination of insurance coverage for workers and retirees. A retiree from the telecommunications company mentioned the termination of supplementary insurance and treatment problems for retirees with special diseases. More details are provided in an interview with an Iran International reporter.

A citizen criticized the increase in food prices in a video sent to Iran International. He said those who did not consider themselves political now have to witness the price hikes. The video highlights growing dissatisfaction with inflation.

Mohammad Saeedi, the Friday prayer leader of Qom, said that people have been present for over 200 nights holding the Islamic Republic flag and demanding revenge against the enemy. He emphasized that the rise of the Islamic front continues and opponents should be prepared for confrontation. He also warned that anyone considering aggression against the Islamic Republic will face a strong response.

Mohammadreza Zanouzi, owner of Tractor club, described Khodadad Azizi's behavior as due to anger and condemned unethical behavior in football. He criticized the media and football federation for not reacting to past insults. Zanouzi called for justice and reform in football conduct.

A report on the living conditions in Iran under political repression and military tensions has been presented. Severe economic problems and social and security pressures are evident. The martyrdom of Mehdi Nosrati Bildashi is also mentioned.

Amnesty International has documented the deadly crackdown on the 'Woman, Life, Freedom' uprising following the death of Mahsa Amini in custody. The report refers to the first part of 'Iran Rising'. The main issue is the death of Mahsa Amini and the subsequent reactions.

Mohammad Javad Haj Ali Akbari stated that no negotiations will take place until the Supreme Leader's conditions are met. He said the enemy is begging for negotiations and sending intermediaries. He also emphasized that Iranian forces have dealt precise blows to the enemy and control of the Strait of Hormuz is in the hands of the Iranian people.

Masoud Pezeshkian emphasized the need for saving gasoline, gas, and electricity consumption during the "Janfdayan Iran" exercise to prevent factory shutdowns. He added that saving energy and using public transportation can disappoint the enemy.
At least 86 illegal hunters and wood smugglers were arrested and referred to judicial authorities in the past week. Meanwhile, 37.7 tons of smuggled wood were discovered and seized.

Istanbul will host the Spanish Super Cup in February 2027. Four teams, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Real Sociedad, and Atletico Madrid, will participate in the competition. The transfer of the matches from Saudi Arabia was due to a scheduling conflict with the Asian Cup.

The mother of Farid Ramazani, who was killed in the December 1404 protests, spoke at his birthday ceremony at his grave. She said, "You are not here to blow out your candle." This video was published on social media.

The Islamic Republic has used a network of individuals active in media and government charity organizations to identify protesters in Khorasan Razavi. This is part of the ongoing investigation into the nationwide protests of December 2025. Farzad Fattahi examines the role of this informant network.

A video released on social media shows family members of one of the martyrs of December 2025 lighting a candle at the grave of Sajad Ghaemi. Sajad Ghaemi is one of the martyrs of the "Woman, Life, Freedom" movement. This act has been reflected in the media.

Jorge Jesus, the new coach of Portugal's national team, announced the first list of players called up to the team. Cristiano Ronaldo is included in the list for the UEFA Nations League matches. Portugal will start their Nations League campaign under Jesus on September 24.

Ahmad Karami-Asad, deputy of the Traffic Police, reported more than 1,609 deaths in intercity road accidents in Shahrivar month. This averages over 50 deaths per day. Temporary closure of some northern routes due to heavy rain was also mentioned.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations center reported that on September 16, 2026, a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz. The incident caused a fire on the deck, which has been controlled and extinguished. All crew members are safe, and environmental impacts have not yet been confirmed.

The President of South Korea stated that no deployment of troops or military equipment leading to participation in war will take place. However, the country may play a greater role in protecting commercial shipping and oil transportation in the region. These remarks were made at a press conference on Friday, September 18.

The mother of Saeed Toklian, a protester killed on January 7, 2026, joined the campaign "One Candle, One Name, One Memory." She stated that she neither forgives nor forgets. This video was published on social media.

Police in Pakistan announced that a bomb explosion in a mosque near a police building in the northwest of the country killed at least 16 people and injured more than 30. No individual or group has claimed responsibility for the attack so far. The report is by Javad Hamdani, a journalist from Iran International.

Asala Nasri performed in Damascus for the first time after more than 15 years. The concert, supported by the Syrian Ministry of Culture, was attended by thousands. She began the program with the song "Paradise of Syria," released after the fall of Bashar al-Assad's government.

Hossein Taeb, head of the Basij Organization, announced that hundreds of thousands of registrants of the "Jan-Fada" campaign in Tehran have been organized and are being integrated into the defense battalions and units. Basic and advanced training courses in land, air, and sea domains have been planned for these individuals. This exercise was held on the morning of Friday, September 27, in Tehran.

The CEO of the Water and Wastewater Company of Markazi Province reported a 12 to 15 percent water loss in urban and rural areas of the province. A significant part of this loss is due to the aging of transmission lines and distribution networks. Lack of funding in recent years has limited the repair and reconstruction of these networks.

A video shows Fatemeh Poursadeghi's son speaking at a birthday ceremony held at his mother's grave. Fatemeh Poursadeghi, 32, was killed by Islamic Republic agents on the night of January 9, 2026, in Rasht. The ceremony was held in her memory.

The Saudi Ministry of Defense announced that the multinational naval defense coalition led by Saudi Arabia has entered an advanced stage of operational readiness. The coalition is preparing to deploy forces and begin naval missions under a unified command. The mission aims to support maritime security and counter threats against shipping routes.

The US State Department has approved visas for the Islamic Republic's delegation to attend the UN General Assembly. Members of this delegation and their families will face restrictions on movement and purchases in New York. They will not be allowed to buy luxury and expensive goods.

The UK government has updated its internal defense plans and emergency preparedness guidelines. Citizens are urged to prepare for severe disruptions in public services, including water and power outages and cyberattacks. People have been asked to stock up on food, water, medicine, and batteries.

The death sentence of Omid Goodarzvand Chegini, a detainee from the January 8 protests in Qazvin, has been confirmed by the appeals court. He is accused of damaging the entrance of the Qazvin governor's office but denies involvement in the destruction. Goodarzvand Chegini is imprisoned in Choubinder prison in Qazvin and was tried without access to a chosen lawyer.

Out of 75 active ambulances in Qom emergency services, 33 are worn out. Additionally, 20 new ambulances supplied with the cooperation of donors and various organizations have not yet been cleared from customs. The Qom 115 emergency service, with 42 bases and nearly 400 personnel, is responsible for pre-hospital emergency response in the province.

Behrouz Kamalvandi, spokesman for the Atomic Energy Organization, said Tehran currently has enough options to defend itself and, regardless of the level of pressures, has the will to overcome the current situation.

Videos released show that children and adolescents, both girls and boys, were widely used with combat weapons in the "Jan-Fadaian" rally in Tehran. In one video, a teenager tells Benjamin Netanyahu that he will assassinate him with a weapon. Another video shows Masoud Pezeshkian among teenagers wearing military uniforms.

The 20th Asian Games in Nagoya will start on Saturday, 28 Shahrivar. Alireza Modiri and Mehdi Kazemi have traveled to Nagoya to cover the competitions. The report reviews the status of the Iranian and Afghan teams and the latest details of the Asian Games.

Ahead of the opening ceremony of the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya, warnings about Typhoon Dujuan and heavy rains have been issued. These conditions have affected the preparation of the ceremony. Additionally, the absence of a central athletes' village has faced criticism.

The Iranian delegation of 522 members has been sent to the Nagoya Asian Games. Among them, 305 are athletes, including 210 men and 95 women competing in 39 sports. Zahra Kiani and Fazel Atrachali will be Iran's flag bearers at the opening ceremony.

Amir Mahdi Keshavarz, a 17-year-old footballer, was killed by two gunshots during protests in the Zibashahr area of Qazvin. His mother expressed her deep sorrow and endless love for her son in an Instagram post. This incident occurred on Friday, January 9, 2026.

Omid Alishah spoke about the conflict and insults by Khodadad Azizi and the support of the Tractor club owner for him. He said that unlike some people who did not observe ethics, he felt vicarious shame. These remarks were made on the sidelines of a charity event for children with cancer.

Women's basketball entered the Asian Games in 1974 in Tehran. The five-member Iranian team experienced its only participation in the history of these games. The Iranian team competed with a combination of young players and was captained by Ziba Aflatoun.

A citizen sent a video showing the unfinished national housing project in Bandar Abbas. He says that money has been taken from people for two years, but the completion of the project has been stopped.

On Sunday, September 12, intelligence agents searched the homes of Majid Ghane and Mehran Basiri, two Baha'i citizens in Yazd. Personal belongings including a laptop and tablet were confiscated during the searches. Additionally, the mobile phones of young people present at Majid Ghane's home were also seized.

The fees for fitness clubs and English classes have increased. Reports include police confrontations with teenagers and issues with insurance and treatment for special patients. Additionally, problems with supplementary insurance and unpaid salaries for pharmacy staff have been mentioned.

Patients with special conditions in Iran reported that the amounts kept for medicine and treatment are recorded as high bank transactions. This issue has occurred amid the ongoing drug shortage and price crisis. More details were reported by Seba Heydarkhani.

The deputy health official of Yazd University of Medical Sciences announced 11 cases of Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever in the province. A 38-year-old woman died due to a hand wound while cutting meat from an unauthorized source. He emphasized the importance of proper meat storage and the dangers of slaughtering animals outside authorized slaughterhouses.

Today, Friday, 27 Shahrivar, a group of job-seeking citizens from Mianrud gathered in front of the Shaheed Beheshti Agro-Industry Company in Dezful. The protesters demanded the hiring of local workers in this company. They called on provincial officials and company managers to pay attention.

Yashar Soltani explained the costs of the Islamic Republic's oil sales network. Each tanker with a capacity of about one million barrels incurs nearly four million dollars in fees and money transfer costs. He said if Iran were connected to SWIFT, this cost would be reduced to about 500 dollars.

Images of the arrest and assault of a teenager in Tabriz have been released, showing violent and humiliating behavior by officers. The Islamic Republic has presented a different narrative by accusing the teenager. This raises questions about the legal treatment of children in custody.

Iran's aviation industry faces multiple crises including expensive tickets, long delays, unpaid staff salaries, and radar issues. Reports of delayed pilot salaries have emerged, and international warnings about Iran's airspace security have raised concerns. Farshad Motaghi discussed these crises in the program "Pivast."

Mohsen Naqvi, Pakistan's Interior Minister, is set to travel to Iran to discuss the escalation of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. The trip will take place in the coming hours. Earlier, Pakistan's army commander had urged Iran to work towards stopping these attacks.

On the fourth anniversary of Mahsa Amini's government killing, Iranians have gathered in Hanover, Germany. Representatives from the federal and state parliaments of Germany and families of the victims of the January 2023 protests are also present at the gathering. A report by Ahmad Samadi, an Iran International journalist, has been published.

The review of the Children's Rights Association's performance in 1404 shows that child sexual abuse is the top issue in the cases referred to the association. These cases include sexual violence and abuse by family members and others, as well as threats and assaults in cyberspace. Despite extensive supervision over sexual matters, the Iranian government has not established a strong support system to protect children from sexual violence.

Farid Ramazani was killed in Tehran on the evening of January 8 by forces of the Islamic Republic. His uncle, who lives in Denmark, said the forces shot Farid and then gave him a coup de grâce. They also targeted the finger with a crown tattoo.

Mehdi Chamran, head of Tehran City Council, said participants of the Janfodayan rally came from various ages and professions to show support for the leadership and the Islamic Republic. He added that the enemy is in decline and will face harsher blows if it continues on its path.

Kylian Mbappé ended his nearly 20-year partnership with Nike and joined the Swiss brand On, becoming the main face of the company's entry into the football shoe market. He also received part of the company's shares. Thierry Henry, as On's football director, played a role in convincing Mbappé to join.

Ahmad Alamolhoda stated in Friday prayers in Mashhad that women without hijab should not be allowed to enter universities as it may lead to gatherings of agitators. He described the university as a sanctuary and called for decisive action by security and judicial authorities. Alamolhoda emphasized that if administrative bodies fail to control the issue, security forces must intervene.

Hossein Ghashghaei, Sara Shamsaei, and Abolfazl Ghashghaei were arrested by security forces nine days ago. Their place of detention and status remain unknown. Hossein and Sara were arrested in Lahijan, and Abolfazl in Zarandieh.

In the first week of the Iranian Women's Premier Football League, Persepolis defeated Tehran 2-0. Esteghlal and Sepahan also won with the same score. Gol Gohar Sirjan beat Varash Nowshahr 4-1 and became the league leader.

The fourth anniversary of the "Woman, Life, Freedom" movement is being held tonight at the main Paris city hall. The event is attended by Iranians living in France, human rights defenders, political activists, and cultural figures. The report and interview were conducted by an Iran International journalist.

Turkey will stop flights of Mahan Air to and from the country starting September 21. This decision follows the sanctioning of three Turkish companies for providing services to Mahan. Turkish officials stated that the ban does not include all Iranian airlines but the risk of cooperation with other companies is being reviewed.

People have reported feeling more comfort and freedom after the removal of mandatory hijab, and the city has become more beautiful. They also mentioned reduced expenses and a change in men's attitudes toward women. This change has made individuals feel more empowered and confident.

Donald Trump stated that the Islamic Republic of Iran wants an agreement with the United States but will not consider it if it is not a good deal. He also said his administration is talking with the Houthis to explore the possibility of a deal. Trump added that Iran is failing financially and militarily, which is why it wants an agreement.

Two separate attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz have been reported. The Islamic Republic stated that one of the ships was passing illegally. Donald Trump also announced that a major decision regarding military operations against the Islamic Republic is approaching.

Mark Carney, the Prime Minister of Canada, is making a historic visit to the Saint Pierre and Miquelon archipelago to meet with Emmanuel Macron. They will discuss cooperation in energy, critical minerals, advanced technologies, and defense coordination. Addressing the impacts of climate change is also part of their talks.

Sara Regensburger, an Iranian-German fashion designer, presented her Spring/Summer 2027 collection titled "Diaspora: The Art of Belonging" at London Fashion Week. The collection is inspired by growing up between two cultures and blends Western tailoring with Iranian details. She also aims to showcase Iranian culture beyond the news.

The US Central Command announced that by September 17, it had redirected 105 commercial ships as part of the US blockade against Iran. CENTCOM released a video showing the USS Boxer operations in the Arabian Sea. The ship and its deployed Marines continue to enforce the blockade.

The mother of Mahna Doukoshkani lit a candle at her daughter's grave as part of the "One Candle, One Name, One Memory" campaign. Mahna Doukoshkani, 18 years old, was shot and killed by officers in Kermanshah on January 8, 2026.

Workers in the service section of Bandar Imam Khomeini Municipality reported non-payment of two months' wages and delays in insurance payments. Workers in the security and executive sections also face wage arrears.

Pete Hegseth, the US Secretary of Defense, described the rescue operation of two American pilots in Iran. One pilot was injured and trapped in a mountainous area. The operation demonstrated the US military's commitment to recovering its personnel.

Yashar Soltani, an Iranian journalist, said in a video interview that Iran's oil sales have been entrusted to four people. He said these four people earned $1.5 billion from discounts on the sale of 80 million barrels of oil alone, apart from their other income from these sales.

The Housing Foundation offices have received funds for war damage compensation but have not paid them. The price of the cancer drug Tedrox has increased from 19 million to 95 million, making it unaffordable for people. Additionally, issues such as delays in car delivery, contaminated tap water in Khalkhal, and unpaid wages at the Marine Engineering and Construction Company have been reported.

Mohammad Radman-Nia, a 29-year-old bodybuilder, was shot on the evening of Friday, January 9, 2026, in the Nezamabad neighborhood of Tehran. He died a day later due to the severity of his injuries. His mother vowed in a video at his grave to continue his path.

Given the developments in Yemen and the insistence of the Islamic Republic on sabotage in Hormuz, the US is preparing for the scenario of restarting attacks. This indicates rising tensions in the region. Further details are not provided in the text.

The spokesperson for the US Treasury Department told Al Jazeera that the department has initiated strict measures against banks supporting Mahan Air in the UAE and Turkey. He added that Turkey and Oman have also suspended Mahan flights.
